analysis.requirement: R2 — Locally-estimated behavioral coefficients: awareness, departure, barrier, and destination-choice parameters must be estimated from local observation/survey data (hierarchical discrete-choice or time-to-departure model, trained and evaluated on held-out data), or all results must be consistently framed as scenario-conditioned projections rather than empirical estimates of Portland unsheltered residents' behavior.
exists_defensible: One genuinely local, event-specific behavioral estimate exists and is implemented: P(aware of shelters at event start) = 0.356 = 26/73, from Hines et al. 2021 'Stories from the Outside' (PSU HRAC, N=73 unhoused Portland-area adults surveyed about THIS September 2020 event), with Wilson 95% CI 0.25-0.47 — registry row V29 (Geography/data/registry/variables.csv:34), implemented as a Bernoulli draw in Geography/src/geography/agents/ELayerSampler.java:39-46 and the UNAWARE state in Geography/src/geography/agents/GisAgent.java:384-393.

A second local behavioral quantity exists as a registered calibration target: P(attempted shelter access | aware) = 0.385 = 10/26 from the same survey — V30 (variables.csv:35), consumed only as the E9 calibration target for the hazard intercept, correctly never asserted as a parameter.

Local demographic marginals for barrier-relevant attributes are sourced: dependents 0.0044 (HUD 2025 PIT CoC OR-501, V33 at variables.csv:38), mobility limitation 0.192 lower bound (2019 Multnomah PIT, V20 at variables.csv:24), age bands (Pathways 2026 N=541 Multnomah, V18 at variables.csv:22), sex (2019 PIT, V19), chronic physical 0.391 (Pathways 2026, V22).

The provenance registry is an unusually disciplined honest ledger: all 55 variable rows carry evidence_class, source, DOI, and sweep range; every departure-hazard coefficient (alphaHazard V38, bRisk/halfLife V36, wOfficial V37, gammaVuln V39, sigmaTheta V35), both destination-choice weights (betaT/betaS, V43 at variables.csv:48), the outreach rate (V41 at variables.csv:46), and all blockage coefficients are explicitly declared ASSUMED with documented anchors and sweep ranges — nothing is disguised as estimated.

The infeasibility of literature transfer is itself documented: 'No study anywhere provides a fitted quantitative choice model for unsheltered people and shelters' (docs/science/phase2-human-agents/04-DECISION.md:84-89), and the project deliberately refused to invent separate pet/belongings/distrust sub-parameters, folding them into one latent construct (04-DECISION.md:91-94) under the F3 governing rule (04-DECISION.md:15-20: every behavioral parameter is sourced or declared class A, swept, and ablated).

Pre-registered prediction discipline covers the behavioral layer: alphaHazard = -8.0 was derived by registered arithmetic to hit the 0.385 attempt target, the realized attempt share was 0.502, and the prediction is scored as a MISS with an appended (not edited) correction of ~ -8.7 (docs/critique-response/13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:20-40).

Baseline-real runs under the sourced awareness value are archived: ER-A/ER-C/ER-D at seeds 42-44 exist in docs/runs/phase-e/ (directory verified) with results documented at 13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:88-133 — the repo has actually executed the scenario-conditioned behavioral analysis the requirement's fallback demands.

The manuscript carries a correct partial hedge: universal awareness makes 'every access figure... an upper bound' and 'the number reaching shelter... is the maximum the geography permits, not the number who would actually arrive' (docs/chapter/Capacity_Is_Not_Access.tex:937-946), plus a dedicated behavioral-scope limitation naming information limits, 211 dispatcher mediation, and rides as unmodeled (tex:1008-1024).
missing: ABSENT: any locally-estimated departure model. All six hazard coefficients are ASSUMED (variables.csv:40-44); the E9 occupancy calibration that would fit the intercept to the one historical occupancy record is deferred on record (13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:82-86) and no E9 run archive exists in docs/runs/ (directory enumeration verified).

ABSENT: any estimated destination-choice model. betaT/betaS are declared assumptions (A-32, variables.csv:48); Cheng 2008 magnitudes are explicitly declared non-transferable ('vehicle-scale... sign and structure only', 04-DECISION.md:166-167); no fitted choice model for this population exists in any literature the project found (04-DECISION.md:84).
ABSENT: outreach-effect data. lambdaOutreachPerDay is 'UNSOURCED — declared assumption (A-31)... a real outreach-contact rate for this event does not exist in the record' (variables.csv:46).

ABSENT: trust, ID-requirement, and transportation mechanisms entirely — the requirement names them, and the model has no trust construct, no ID gate, and no transport mode of any kind (walking is the only movement; grep of Geography/src confirms no transport code path). The barrier set is belongings/pet/dependents only (GisAgent.java:934-944 region per inventory; variables.csv:36-38,45).

ABSENT: a hierarchical discrete-choice or time-to-departure model estimated on a training sample and evaluated for calibration/predictive error on held-out data. No estimation dataset exists that could support it: the entire event-specific behavioral record is one newspaper occupancy snapshot (~90 + ~40 of 198 beds, one night) and the N=73 retrospective survey (04-DECISION.md:65-80, which states these are 'the only quantitative behavioural calibration targets this project has').
ABSENT: held-out evaluation of any behavioral component. The single occupancy observation is used as a censored bracket check (1.5-15.6x), not a fit; there is no second observation to hold out.

ABSENT: local estimates of barrier costs (0.10-0.42 log-odds anchors transferred from Tanim 2022 general-household evacuation meta-analysis, variables.csv:45) and of smoke-severity response magnitude (z_R form from Castillo 2023 Oregon housed households, magnitude unsourced, variables.csv:41).

ABSENT from the manuscript: any of the local behavioral evidence or the behavioral-layer results. The tex never cites Hines et al., never states the 0.356/0.385 values, and presents 'a model of awareness' as future work (tex:1069-1074) even though an implemented, locally-sourced awareness layer with archived runs exists in the same repo.
implementable_with_existing_data: Awareness-interval reporting for the headline arms: pAwareInit is an implemented parameter (ELayerSampler.java:44-46); sweeping it over the sourced Wilson CI 0.25-0.47 (variables.csv:34) across arms A/B/C would convert every absolute access figure from a single upper bound into an interval — exactly the extension tex:1069-1074 names as most valuable, requiring zero new data.

E9 calibration of alphaHazard: fit the hazard intercept so the realized attempt share among the aware matches 0.385 (V30) and/or so historical-reference occupancy brackets the ~90/40-of-99 targets, using the existing 2020 configuration (Geography/data/shelters/shelters_2020-09.csv, docs/runs/historical-reference/ n=2037 setup) and the class-C protocol already specified with target/fit/residual reporting (04-DECISION.md:131-134). The corrected value ~ -8.7 is already computed (13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:37-40) but not adopted.

Behavioral-conditioning section for the manuscript from archived runs: the ER-A/C/D baseline-real results (docs/runs/phase-e/, results at 13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:88-133) already show that under measured awareness ~17.8% shelter, the A-to-C placement gap disappears (0-1 residents vs 47 seed noise), the mobility gap inverts, and arm D's triage reserve arbitrates nothing — all of which can be reported now as the scenario-conditioned counterpoint to the universal-awareness arms.

Global sensitivity analysis over the assumed behavioral coefficients: all ~15 assumed coefficients carry registered sweep ranges in variables.csv (rows 34-56); a Latin-hypercube or fractional-factorial design under common random numbers (already proposed at 04-DECISION.md:223) needs only the existing model and registry.

Consistent scenario-conditioned reframing of the manuscript (the requirement's explicit fallback): editorial pass replacing present-tense empirical phrasings with conditioned ones, using the hedge language that already exists at tex:937-946 and md:287-289 — no data required.

Wachinger-constraint and barrier-gradient reporting from existing archives: the phase-e runs already quantify barrier effects on departure (sheltered share 19.1% no barriers / 11.5% one / 0.0% two-plus; ~87% of high-barrier residents never depart even at peak PM2.5 — 13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:117-120), publishable now as scenario-conditioned barrier results.
needs_new_empirical_data: Destination-choice coefficients (walking time, pet policy, belongings storage, ID requirements, trust): a stated-choice/discrete-choice-experiment survey of Portland unsheltered residents, administered through peer-researcher/outreach partnerships (the Street Roots Ambassadors model Hines et al. used), with shelter attributes as experimental factors.

Time-to-departure under smoke: prospective intake logging at clean-air shelter activations (arrival timestamps linked to concurrent hourly PM2.5), requiring a data agreement with the Joint Office of Homeless Services before the next activation — the only way to estimate a real hazard model.

Outreach effect on departure: linked outreach-contact logs and subsequent intake records (contact-to-arrival panel) collected during an activation; no contact-rate record exists for any event (variables.csv:46).

Awareness with tighter precision and channel decomposition: a probability-anchored survey module (e.g., attached to the PIT count) re-measuring shelter awareness and information channels at larger N than 73, to shrink the 0.25-0.47 interval and estimate information-source effects.

Individual-level barrier-outcome data: an intercept/panel survey after a smoke event that records, per person, barriers (pet, belongings, mobility, ID, trust) jointly with whether shelter was attempted and reached — the existing Hines aggregates are marginals and cannot support joint coefficient estimation.
needs_external_acquisition: JOHS/Multnomah County after-action report and any nightly occupancy or intake logs for the September 2020 clean-air shelters — candidate source: Joint Office of Homeless Services / Multnomah County records request; the repo documents these were never obtained (docs/final/SHELTER_CAPACITY_AUDIT.md:158-166 per validation inventory). Multiple occupancy nights would convert the single calibration point into a fittable time series.

Hines et al. 2021 survey microdata (individual-level awareness x attempt x barriers) — candidate source: PSU Homelessness Research & Action Collaborative; would support joint estimation of awareness and attempt with covariates instead of two marginal ratios.

211info call records for September 2020 (volumes, timestamps, shelter-referral outcomes) — candidate source: 211info; the current evidence base for the information channel is one newspaper sentence (21 calls on Sept 15; 04-DECISION.md:71).

HMIS intake records for the event window and for present-day shelters — candidate source: Multnomah County HMIS administrator; individual arrivals with demographics would support a covariate-adjusted time-to-departure model and held-out evaluation across sites or days.

Pathways Study 2026 microdata (shelter-use history: 67% used a shelter in 6 months, 34% most often) — candidate source: PSU HRAC / OHSU study team; would provide a revealed-preference baseline for present-day shelter choice against which stated-choice estimates could be validated.

County shelter-occupancy dashboard time series — candidate source: Multnomah County (the dashboard existed but was not machine-readable at audit time per SHELTER_CAPACITY_AUDIT.md:50-53 as cited in the validation inventory); a per-facility nightly series would enable calibration and hold-out testing of any occupancy-generating model.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'The present system shelters 30.1% of residents' (and md variants 'The present 36-facility system shelters 30.1% of residents')
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Present-tense declarative about the real Portland system, but the number is a model output under universal awareness, omniscient nearest-shelter choice, and instant compliance. The repo's own archived baseline-real runs at the sourced local awareness value (0.356) yield ~17.8% sheltered (13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:101-104), so the figure is not robust to the one behavioral coefficient that IS locally estimated. The hedge exists elsewhere (tex:937-946) but this sentence carries no conditioning.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: The awareness limitation 'applies identically to all three scenarios, so it does not affect the comparison between them, which is what this chapter claims'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Contradicted by the repo's own archived experiment: under measured awareness the A-to-C comparison itself disappears — sheltered counts differ by 0-1 residents against 47 of seed noise (P-E2, 13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:105-106), and 'the binding constraint moves from architecture to behaviour' (13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:125-133). The claim that the comparison is awareness-invariant is asserted, was testable with repo assets, was in fact tested, and failed — yet the manuscript does not disclose this.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'reserving 10% of each facility's spaces for mobility-limited arrivals takes the gap to zero at identical total admissions and zero capital cost' and the policy sentence 'the triage reserve buys the same equity for free'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: A policy recommendation stated without behavioral conditioning. Under the sourced awareness value, arm D records zero capacity refusals, 'the 667 reserved beds arbitrate nothing and ER-D is not a test of triage at all' (13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:109-116) — a caveat the phase-E document says 'must be stated wherever ER-D is reported', and the manuscript's triage claims never carry it.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: Mobility-limited residents 'remain the worst-served group throughout' / equity statements said to 'survive every measure'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Conditional on the no-behavior arms. Under the sourced-awareness runs the mobility gap inverts (limited 17.0% vs unimpaired 15.7%, P-E4, 13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:109-111), because when departure rather than capacity binds, slower walkers are no longer outcompeted. 'Throughout' and 'every measure' quantify only over scenarios that exclude the behavioral layer.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'A model of awareness is the most valuable single addition... would give the model a parameter that could be fitted if occupancy data ever becomes available'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Understates the evidence state in the opposite direction: an implemented awareness layer with a locally sourced value (0.356, ELayerSampler.java:46), a sourced attempt target (0.385), and nine archived baseline-real runs already exist in the repo (docs/runs/phase-e/). Presenting this as hypothetical future work lets the manuscript avoid reporting that its headline conclusions do not survive the sourced value — a reviewer who finds the phase-E documents will read this as selective disclosure.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: 'the same 6,842 spaces more than halve refusals depending only on placement' and the central-result framing '550 people were refused shelter during an event in which the system held exactly one space per person'
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Refusal counts are artifacts of the universal-awareness, instant-departure regime in which all 6,842 residents converge on shelters; under measured awareness (~1,220 departures) system capacity never binds and refusals-by-capacity approach zero (13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:125-133). The unconditioned phrasing reads as an empirical estimate of refusals during an event, which the requirement forbids.

proposed_methods: Awareness-bracketed headline reporting: re-run A/B/C with pAwareInit swept over the Wilson CI 0.25-0.47 plus the universal-awareness bound, and report every access/refusal figure as an interval indexed by awareness — the minimal defensible closure using only existing code and data.

Bayesian calibration (ABC or binomial likelihood) of alphaHazard and bRisk jointly against the two local targets (site occupancies ~90/40 of 99; attempt share 10/26), with posterior predictive checks and residual reporting per the class-C protocol already specified at 04-DECISION.md:131-134; report posterior intervals, never point estimates.

Global sensitivity analysis (Sobol indices or fractional-factorial under common random numbers, as proposed at 04-DECISION.md:223) over all assumed behavioral coefficients using the registered sweep ranges in variables.csv, with variance decomposition identifying which manuscript conclusions are assumption-driven versus data-driven.

If HMIS/occupancy series are acquired: a discrete-time survival model (complementary log-log hazard) of shelter arrival with time-varying PM2.5, barrier, and mobility covariates, trained on a subset of days or sites and evaluated on the held-out remainder via calibration plots and Brier score — the time-to-departure model the requirement names.

If new survey data are collected: hierarchical Bayes multinomial logit on stated-choice tasks (attributes: walk time, pet policy, belongings storage, ID requirement, staffing/trust proxies), validated against Pathways revealed shelter-use shares; partial-pooling across mobility and barrier strata to handle small subgroup n.

If Hines microdata are acquired: joint bivariate-probit or hierarchical logistic estimation of awareness and attempt with respondent covariates, replacing the two marginal ratios; propagate the joint posterior through the ABM by forward simulation.

Manuscript fallback (implementable immediately and required if estimation remains infeasible): a systematic editorial pass converting present-tense access/refusal/equity sentences to scenario-conditioned form ('under universal awareness and immediate compliance, the modeled system admits...'), plus a behavioral-conditioning subsection reporting the archived ER results and stating explicitly which conclusions (the scarcity-band equity findings, the placement effect, the triage recommendation) are conditional on demand exceeding behavioral uptake.
analysis.priority_rationale: This requirement is maximally load-bearing for this project, and uniquely so, because the repo itself has already run the experiment that shows why: with the single behavioral coefficient that IS locally estimated (awareness 0.356 from the event-specific PSU survey), the manuscript's entire headline structure collapses — 30.1%/91.6%/96.0% becomes ~17.8% across all arms, the A-to-C placement effect disappears into seed noise, the 550-refusal central result cannot occur because capacity never binds, the mobility equity gap inverts, and the triage-reserve policy recommendation becomes untestable (docs/runs/phase-e/ ER arms; 13-PHASE-E-PREDICTIONS.md:88-133). So R2 is not a robustness footnote: it decides whether the manuscript's claims are about Portland or about a geometry counterfactual. The project's position is defensible in parts a reviewer will credit — the registry honestly classes every hazard, choice, barrier, and outreach coefficient as assumed with sweep ranges; the infeasibility of local estimation is genuinely documented (one occupancy night, one N=73 retrospective survey, no fitted choice model in any literature); and the fallback the requirement offers (scenario-conditioned framing) is largely achieved in the limitations sections. What fails review today is the asymmetry: present-tense empirical phrasings in the abstract and summary, an explicit claim that the comparison is awareness-invariant which the repo's own archived runs disconfirm, and the presentation of the implemented, locally-sourced awareness layer as hypothetical future work. The highest-priority fixes are cheap and internal — awareness-bracketed reporting, the E9 one-parameter calibration, disclosure of the ER baseline-real results, and the editorial conditioning pass — while genuine local estimation (survival model on intake logs, DCE for choice coefficients) requires data acquisition from JOHS/HMIS/PSU that the repo shows was never obtained.
